newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean won ends higher after BOK interventions.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean won ends higher after BOK interventions.

text.p: The won ended Wednesday higher against the dollar after multiple interventions by the central bank, aimed at preventing the local currency from falling further, traders said.
The won closed at 821.30, after opening at a low of 823.50.
"Banks were eager to cover their short dollar positions, boosting the currency yesterday and early this morning. But the central bank was determined to support the won," said a foreign bank dealer.
The Bank of Korea was seen intervening three times on Wednesday, at 823.00, 821.60 and again at 821.30, dealers said.
The central bank has never confirmed that it intervenes in the market.
Despite the central bank's active dollar sales, traders said there was still demand for the U.S. currency.
"I think the dollar will move between 821 and 823 tomorrow, unless the central bank really aggressively comes in," said a Western trader.
Other dealers were more cautious, putting Thursday's range at between 820.00 and 822.00.
Thursday's mid-rate is expected to be pegged at 821.10 against 820.00 today.-- KATHERINE BRUCE (822) 727 5644
